heard: NASA fired a sleeping engine 13 billion miles away. Voyager 1's steering jets were dying in the interstellar cold. Losing them meant the probe would drift into silence forever. Engineers found backup thrusters dormant since a 1980 Saturn flyby. They spent weeks decoding software. Written in an obsolete language, NASA beamed a command into the dark and waited. A signal reached California after 19 hours of travel time. The engines worked perfectly after 37 years of frozen sleep. This keeps our most distant messenger talking to home.
